subject: Genetics
title: Repetitive DNA
description: Learn Repetitive DNA in one minute.

hook.text: Nearly half your genome is made of repeating sequences—the same patterns copied thousands of times. Why?

buildup.text: Alu elements alone appear over a million times. LINE-1 elements make up 17% of your DNA. Repeats everywhere.

discovery.text: Many repeats are ancient viruses that inserted themselves into our ancestors' DNA millions of years ago.

twist.text: Some repeats aren't parasites—they drive evolution. They create new genes by reshuffling existing DNA segments.

climax.text: Repetitive DNA is a molecular fossil record. It tells the story of our genome's evolution over millions of years.

punchline.text: Half your DNA is ancient copy-paste. And it matters.

quiz.question: What fraction of the human genome is repetitive DNA?
